content.text:
Let me understand the rule from the verifier.

`partition(I)` groups all cells by color value (each color becomes one object, potentially disconnected).

`x1 = fork(recolor, color, backdrop)` — for each color object, compute its bounding box (backdrop) and recolor to that color. So each color's bounding box is filled with that color.

`x3 = mfilter(x2, hline)` — keep only objects whose bounding box is a horizontal line (height 1, width = len). Actually hline checks width(patch)==len(patch) and height(patch)==1. Here patch is the recolored object (filled bbox), len = number of cells in bbox. So hline means the bbox is a single row.

`x4 = mfilter(x2, vline)` — bbox single column.

Then paint I with x3 (horizontal lines) first, then paint with x4 (vertical lines) on top. So vertical lines overwrite horizontal lines.

So: For each color, find the bounding box of all cells of that color. If the bounding box is a horizontal line (one row), draw it. If vertical (one column), draw it. Vertical drawn after horizontal, so vertical on top.

Also colors with a single cell: their bbox is 1x1, which satisfies both hline and vline (height==1,width==1, len==1). So a single cell stays.

Colors whose bbox is a rectangle larger than 1x1 (both dims >1) are ignored.

tools.name: show_example

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

output_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Show the Student a labeled input-output pair that you authored. If your output matches the rule, the pair is shown and you receive a success acknowledgement only. If it does not match, the pair is not shown and you receive the gold output so you can correct it.

tools.name: show_transformed_input

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Provide only an input grid. The environment applies the verifier and shows the resulting gold input-output pair to the student.

tools.name: query_student

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Probe the student with an input of your choice. You receive the student's predicted output, the gold output, and whether they matched. The student does not see the gold pair unless you later show it with show_example or show_transformed_input.

tools.name: start_exam
tools.description: End teaching and send the student to the exam: they must solve held-out generator inputs (unseen in demonstrations or probes) with the history so far. No further teaching after this.

tools.name: propose_inputs
tools.description: Submit candidate input grids you might show, several at once. The environment keeps the ones the verifier accepts, notes which leave the grid unchanged under the rule, and ranks the rest as candidates. Free: nothing is shown until you call show_transformed_input.
